## Teaching scope

All records are invented. The six regression paths illustrate decisions rather
than actual findings, valid specification-curve inference or causal effects.
The TOST numbers are separate normal-model teaching scenarios.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
from IPython.display import Markdown, SVG, display
import research

results = research.run_project()
mean_score = round(results["summary"]["mean_score"], 3)
n_records = results["summary"]["n"]
```

## Data and computations

This run contains `{python} n_records` synthetic records, with a mean score of
`{python} mean_score` points. These numbers come from the code cell rather than
manually typed results. The dictionary defines units and illustrative quality
flags; it does not license exclusion rules for a real study.

```{python}
lines = ["| Quality rule | Model | n | Hours coefficient |",
         "| --- | --- | --- | --- |"]
for path in results["paths"]:
    lines.append(f'| {path["quality_rule"]} | {path["specification"]} | '
                 f'{path["n"]} | {path["beta_hours"]:.6f} |')
display(Markdown("\n".join(lines)))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-paths
#| fig-cap: "Six descriptive OLS paths on entirely synthetic teaching data."
display(SVG(filename=str(research.ROOT / "outputs/specification.svg")))
```

## Limitations and reporting

The coefficient changes with both the sample rule and the baseline adjustment.
No confidence intervals or empirical claims are made. A file hash links this run
to its exact input. Rendering Word/PDF and RTL typography requires the relevant
engine, fonts and format-specific checking; these outputs are not prevalidated
by the supplied Python tests.
